claim: Socratic interrogation (clarification, causal probing, counterexample-based interrogation) improves physical consistency, hypothesis completeness, uncertainty calibration, and downstream experimental-plan validity compared to generic review, which improves surface-level completeness but is less effective at exposing missing causal links or specifying conditions under which a conclusion could fail.
falsifier: One could implement a multi-agent system with a Socratic questioning module and a generic review module, then compare the quality of generated hypotheses and experimental plans on a set of scientific problems.

conditions: in the context of multi-agent autonomous scientific discovery
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported multi-agent system (Duzhi) and the specific experimental tasks; transfer beyond these conditions is unestablished.

title: Socratic interrogation–physical consistency, hypothesis completeness…
